## Natural history notes

A small odorous ant characterized by its dark reddish-brown to black body, smooth shiny gaster, and tendency to release a noticeable odor when disturbed or crushed. In Florida, it is associated with wet, open or semi-open habitats such as bogs, marshes, wet prairies, pine flatwoods, and swamp edges, where it nests in soil, leaf litter, grass clumps, hollow stems, or decaying vegetation. It forages for small insects, honeydew, nectar, and other sugary resources, while helping move nutrients through wetland soils and serving as prey for spiders, birds, and other insect-eating animals.
